reason: I ranked the small active-loop changes first. Fusing the decrement with the branch is a bounded test; moving pointer updates between FMOPA operations is also a limited schedule change. Both target the active panel32 path and preserve K order, though neither has measured support. The lookahead schedule may hide load latency, but its prologue and drain add bounds and correctness risk. Prefetch is easy to test but may add instruction cost; the earlier inactive-path prefetch regressed, which does not predict this path. A 4 KiB scratch microbuffer adds K-block loop work without reducing packing volume. Padding has no demonstrated cache-conflict basis and increases scratch size. Packing B adds timed work; full B-panel packing adds substantially more memory traffic. Transpose fusion requires a more invasive assembly change. The A transpose proposal affects fallback sizes, not the measured n=512 path. No proposal has evidence of a repeatable gain, and noisy prior scores do not identify causes.
